key_insight: An AI system can automatically extract discourse features from movie narrations and distinguish aphasia from healthy control speech with excellent accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This approach could make discourse assessment more scalable and ecologically valid in clinical settings by reducing the manual effort needed to score patient narratives.
method: Used a vision-language model to generate main concept inventories directly from each movie clip’s video, audio, and subtitles
Extracted macrolinguistic features such as main concept completeness and sentiment, plus microlinguistic features including fluency, lexical, and syntactic measures
Evaluated classification performance and correlations with aphasia severity in control and aphasia groups
evidence_signal: In 51 controls and 54 people with aphasia, the discourse features achieved AUC=0.95 for group classification, with strong effect sizes and severity correlations reported in the abstract.
watch_item: Clinical deployment will still depend on robust validation across diverse speakers, languages, and stimulus sets, since automated inventories must remain accurate and fair in real-world use.
paper_title: Assessing spoken discourse in aphasia using multimodal artificial intelligence
